query:
Define a two-parameter family of kernels
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Kepsdef}
K_{\epsilon,\eta}(t)\equiv \Big(1+\epsilon |t|+\eta t^2\Big)\,K_0(t)
=\left(1+\epsilon |t|+\eta t^2\right)\frac{1}{2\sinh(|t|/2)},
\end{equation}
and the corresponding operator $\mathcal{K}_{\epsilon,\eta}$ by the same rule as \eqref{eq:K0def}.
Derive the eigenvalue
\[
\chi_{\epsilon,\eta}(\nu)
\quad\text{defined by}\quad
(\mathcal{K}_{\epsilon,\eta}\phi_\nu)(\rho)=\chi_{\epsilon,\eta}(\nu)\phi_\nu(\rho),
\]
as an explicit expression in terms of $\chi_0(\nu)$ and its derivatives up to fourth order:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:target_form}
\chi_{\epsilon,\eta}(\nu)=\chi_0(\nu)\;+\;\epsilon\,(\cdots)\;+\;\eta\,(\cdots).
\end{equation}
response:
on is not \(-\chi_0''(\nu)\).

FINAL RESULT:
\[
\boxed{\chi_{\epsilon,\eta}(\nu)=\chi_0(\nu)-\epsilon\pi^2\tanh^2(\pi\nu)+\eta\left[-\chi_0''(\nu)-28\zeta(3)\right].}
\]
The \(\epsilon\) term follows from the trigamma reflection formula. The \(\eta\) term follows from two Fourier derivatives and the subtraction at \(\nu=0\); the coefficients of \(\chi_0^{(3)}\) and \(\chi_0^{(4)}\) are both \(0\).
